Bhāmaha
(14th cent.)

See AIOC. XXIII. i. 43.

Bhāmaha
earliest rhetorician; hailed from Kashmir; son of Kakrila Gomin; earlier than Daṇḍin; belonged to mid. 6th century.
q. by several writers on alaṅk.; q. by Ānanadavardhana in Dhvanyāloka; by Abhinavagupta in Locana; by Nārāyana in his C. on Vṛttaratnākara.
See ABORI. Golden Jubilee Vol.. XLVIII an. XLIX. p.. 276 ff.; also Encyc. Dict. of Skt. Lit. p.. 152-53; also Kane, HSP. p.. 78-88; For a comparative study of Bhāmaha an. Daṇḍin, see ibid. p.. 102-33; Keith, A. B. Daṇḍin an. Bhāmaha, [Page016a] Ind. Studies in honour of C. R. Lanman, p.. 167-85; also M. T. Narasimhaiyengar, JRAS. (1905). p.. 535-45.
-Kāvyālaṅkārasūtra or Bhāmahālaṅkāra. See under the text.
